name: Agent KB (AGENT KB) - Leveraging Cross-Domain Experience for Agentic Problem Solving
venue: Accepted at CFAgentic @ ICML'25 Workshop (Oral; Best Paper Runner-Up Award). Primary public artifact is arXiv:2507.06229 (cs.CL/cs.AI); submitted 8 Jul 2025, last revised 27 Oct 2025 (v5). The arXiv title is 'Agent KB: Leveraging Cross-Domain Experience for Agentic Problem Solving'; the OpenReview workshop version is titled 'AGENT KB: A Hierarchical Memory Framework for Cross-Domain Agentic Problem Solving' (OpenReview id ohXoWHlrn8).
authors_affiliation: Xiangru Tang, Tianrui Qin, Tianhao Peng (co-first authors), Ziyang Zhou, Daniel Shao, Tingting Du, Xinming Wei, Peng Xia, Fang Wu, He Zhu, Ge Zhang, Jiaheng Liu, Xingyao Wang, Sirui Hong, Chenglin Wu, Hao Cheng, Chi Wang, Wangchunshu Zhou (senior). Affiliations: Yale University, OPPO (OPPO-PersonalAI), UW-Madison, UNC Chapel Hill, Stanford University, Bytedance, Nanjing University, All Hands AI, DeepWisdom, Microsoft Research, Google DeepMind.
code_url: https://github.com/OPPO-PersonalAI/Agent-KB (official; Apache-2.0; ~431 stars as of mid-2025; Python-dominant. Contains Agent-KB-GAIA (smolagents/open_deep_research) and Agent-KB-SWE-bench subprojects). Anonymous reproducibility mirror cited in paper: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/Agent-KB/
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/OPPO-PersonalAI/Agent-KB (official repo; last push Aug 2025). No separate maintained leaderboard/paper-list.
task_domain: Agentic problem solving spanning reasoning and software engineering: general/long-horizon tool-use and web research QA (GAIA), expert/scientific QA (Humanity's Last Exam Bio/Chem, GPQA), and code repair (SWE-bench Lite). Cross-domain experience transfer across heterogeneous agent frameworks (planning + tool-use + code).
problem_setting: Inference-time, training-free (no retraining/fine-tuning) memory layer that enables experience sharing across multiple heterogeneous agent frameworks (smolagents, OWL, SWE-Agent, OpenHands). Interactive multi-pass agentic solving: each task is attempted in three sequential passes (pass@1 retrieves cross-task experiences; pass@2 enriches Agent KB with failure diagnoses from the first attempt; pass@3 revisits unresolved cases with the expanded pool). Supervision is task-level outcome (exact-match correctness / SWE-bench test passage); both successful and failed runs are normalized into experiences. The knowledge base is bootstrapped offline from 80 human seed trajectories plus automatic rollouts (~9.5k experiences) and continues to grow online across passes/frameworks. Frameworks contribute to and consume the same shared KB via lightweight REST/RPC APIs without architectural changes.
what_is_retrieved: Structured 'experiences' distilled from heterogeneous agent trajectories: (a) workflow-level experiences = high-level reusable problem-solving strategies/plans and agent_experience guideline lists (planning stage), and (b) execution-level experiences/snippets = targeted diagnostic fixes and correction hints derived from execution traces (feedback stage). Each experience unit E = <pi, gamma, S, C> = (task embedding, goal-constraint predicates, action-reasoning pairs {(a_i, r_i)}, cross-framework metadata).
retrieval_grounding: HYBRID: a structured experience knowledge base that is bootstrapped offline (human seeds + automatic rollouts over benchmark datasets) and GROWS online during multi-pass deployment as frameworks write back new experiences (additions, conflict resolution, eviction). It is the agent ecosystem's own distilled trajectory memory rather than a static external document corpus; tool-level web search exists in the base agents but the defining retrieval targets the shared experience KB.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k retrieval (default top-k = 3; SWE-bench retrieve prompt asks for 3-5 entries). After hybrid scoring/reranking the top-k candidates are deduplicated, then refined. The objective is precision-driven small-set selection: ablation (Fig 5b) shows hybrid retrieval peaks around k=3 and remains robust across top-k settings; it is not a recall/completeness objective over a minimal needed set.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve, Reuse(=Refine/adapt), Revise(=feedback-driven refinement), Retain(=write-back)] - the paper explicitly restructures the classic CBR Retrieve-Reuse-Revise-Retain cycle into a Reason-Retrieve-Refine loop with cross-agent write-back. Mapping: Retrieve = hybrid BM25+embedding retrieval; Reuse/Revise = Refine step adapts (entity mapping, tool substitution, step reordering) plus feedback-stage diagnostic correction; Retain = self-evolving memory addition/dedup/eviction with utility scores. All four phases are effectively realized.
explicit_cbr_grounding: Partial/True-with-reframing. The work explicitly references case-based reasoning for LLM agents (cites Hatalis et al. 2025 'Review of case-based reasoning for LLM agents') and the classic Retrieve-Reuse-Revise-Retain cycle, but deliberately reframes its own pipeline as a 'Reason-Retrieve-Refine loop with write-back across agents' rather than branding itself as CBR. It does not center Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner as its primary framing; it positions itself as a cross-framework shared memory infrastructure that restructures the CBR cycle.
retrieval_unit: Structured experience unit (a distilled problem-solution-experience case): E = <pi (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 task embedding), gamma (goal-constraint predicates), S = {(a_i, r_i)} action-reasoning pairs, C (cross-framework metadata)>. Surfaced either as a workflow-level reusable plan/guideline (planning) or an execution-pattern fix/hint (feedback). Effectively (question, agent_plan/agent_experience, [search_agent_plan/experience]) JSON entries.
index_source: Hybrid construction. Offline bootstrap: 80 human seed trajectories (60 BrowseComp/HopRAG-style browsing + 20 SWE-Gym-style coding) drive automatic rollouts by smolagents/OWL/SWE-Agent/OpenHands over BrowseComp, MultiHopRAG, HLE, WebWalkerQA, RepoClassBench, SWE-Gym-Raw, RepoEval, yielding ~9k workflow summaries + ~7k execution snippets (~9.5k experience entries). Online growth: the same KB is enriched at test time across passes (failure diagnoses added in pass@2/3) and across frameworks via shared APIs.
index_structure_topology: Flat experience store with a calibrated hybrid index: a lexical (BM25) inverted index over text plus a dense vector index of all-MiniLM-L6-v2 task embeddings, fused by a weighted score (alpha=0.5). Entries carry framework-compatibility metadata C and goal-constraint predicates gamma used as filters. Conceptually 'hierarchical' in that it stores workflow-level vs execution-level (planning vs feedback) experiences, but the retrievable structure is a metadata-keyed flat hybrid index rather than a knowledge graph.
retriever_type: Hybrid: lexical BM25 shortlisting + dense semantic ranking (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 sentence-transformer embeddings, cosine), combined via calibrated weighted score fusion (sigma_hyb = alpha * sigma_text + (1-alpha) * sigma_sem, alpha=0.5). An LLM is used as a ranker/curator during deduplication (knowledge curation) but the retrieval scorer itself is BM25 + embedding hybrid.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf) for the retriever: BM25 and a frozen all-MiniLM-L6-v2 encoder; the hybrid fusion weight alpha and disagreement-gate threshold beta are fixed hyperparameters (0.5 / 0.8), not learned. The only learned/adaptive signal is at the memory-management level: each stored experience maintains a utility score u_j <- u_j + eta(r_j - u_j) updated from a reward signal r_j (retrieval success / execution gain) to drive eviction - a value/utility update over entries, not a trained retrieval policy.
query_construction: Reason step constructs the query. Planning stage: the Reason module reads the task description, surfaces key requirements/challenges and produces structured queries (keyword/concept lists, e.g. 'EC numbers; virus testing method; SPFMV; SPCSV; ...') targeting reusable subroutines/success patterns. Feedback stage: the Reason module analyzes execution traces/critic highlights to derive queries from observed errors (rather than the task description). So queries are LLM-reasoned/intent-extracted and decomposed into searchable components, distinct per stage.
query_granularity: Two-level / dual-phase: a task-level query at the planning stage (one query from the task description per pass), and a trajectory/feedback-level query at the feedback stage (derived from execution traces and critic highlights). Re-issued across the three sequential passes. Not per-CoT-step or per-token.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative across two fixed stages per attempt and across three sequential passes: retrieve at the planning stage (before/while forming the plan) and again at the feedback stage (after initial execution, conditioned on error traces). Within a benchmark instance, this repeats over pass@1/pass@2/pass@3. It is a fixed two-stage schedule, not uncertainty-triggered active retrieval and not a learned router.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule tied to pipeline stage: (1) planning stage trigger = arrival of a new task description; (2) feedback stage trigger = completion of an execution attempt whose trace/critic indicates errors/bottlenecks (re-engaged for unresolved cases in pass@2/pass@3). No token-level confidence, attention/uncertainty, learned complexity classifier, or reflection-token trigger.
reranking: Yes. After BM25 lexical shortlisting, candidates are reranked by semantic task similarity (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) and combined via calibrated weighted hybrid fusion (alpha=0.5), i.e. a weighted-score fusion reranking; top-k are then deduplicated. An LLM ranker is additionally used during memory deduplication/curation (comparing reasoning quality, completeness, transferability) but that is for write-time curation, not query-time reranking.
retrieved_context_refinement: Refine stage + dedup. Retrieved candidates are not replayed verbatim; the Refine step adapts abstract action patterns to currently available tools/APIs using metadata C, and when multiple experiences are retrieved it synthesizes them into one coherent workflow via entity mapping, tool substitution, and step reordering. A disagreement gate filters feedback-stage refinements. Top-k candidates are deduplicated before refinement. (rerank + decompose/recompose + adaptation + gating).
tool_document_engineering: N/A for tool indexing. Agent KB indexes distilled experiences, not tool/API documents. Tool/API compatibility is handled at refine time via standardized action vocabularies and metadata C (tool substitution / entity mapping) rather than via synthetic-query augmentation or instruction-tuned tool embeddings.
index_content_separation: Yes (partial). The KB exposes lightweight REST/RPC APIs and stores compact structured experience units (task embedding pi + predicates gamma + metadata C + action-reasoning pairs S) that are retrieved cheaply, while the heavy native execution happens in the base framework. It separates workflow-level (planning) experiences from execution-level (feedback) snippets, and curated human seeds are stored but never retrieved directly (they only seed generation), giving a lightweight-index-then-content flavour.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Live, evolving experience store synchronized across frameworks via lightweight REST endpoints / RPC calls (submit + retrieve experiences); experiences gathered in one framework become instantly available to others. Self-evolving with CRUD-like operations (addition, LLM-ranked conflict resolution/deduplication, utility-based eviction). Integration protocol is HTTP/REST + RPC APIs (not RapidAPI/MCP); it is a tool-agnostic memory service rather than a tool registry.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A. Retrieval does not model inter-tool dependency graphs or prerequisites. Cross-framework tool compatibility is handled heuristically at refine time (tool substitution, entity mapping, step reordering using metadata C), not via a dependency graph or dependency-aware reranking.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation + case/experience adaptation. Retrieved experiences are injected as concise actionable suggestions/guidelines that (a) seed the agent's initial plan with cross-domain workflows (planning stage) and (b) supply targeted diagnostic fixes applied to live execution (feedback stage). The base agent is left unchanged; Agent KB intercepts only the planning and feedback points. No training signal / no weight updates (training-free).
planning_integration: Plan-then-retrieve-then-refine, dual-phase and looped with execution. Planning stage: Reason summarizes the task -> Retrieve selects experiences -> Refine synthesizes them into an executable plan rho returned to the native framework. The framework executes; then the Feedback stage runs a second Reason-Retrieve-Refine cycle over the execution trace to produce a refined plan rho', gated by the disagreement gate. Repeated across pass@1/2/3. Retrieval interfaces at plan time and post-execution feedback time, not inside MCTS/tree search.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-stage / per-pass: one retrieval+refine at planning (per-plan) and one at feedback (per-execution-trace), repeated across three passes. Coarser than per-CoT-step or per-token interleaving; closer to per-answer/per-attempt with a planning vs feedback split.
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted adaptation + execution-feedback-driven revision. Retrieved experiences are adapted (not replayed) in the Refine step via entity mapping, tool substitution, and step reordering to fit available tools/APIs and domain constraints; the feedback stage performs execution-feedback-driven revision of the plan, and a disagreement gate (cosine of plan embeddings >= beta=0.8) blocks revisions that diverge too far from the original plan. No RL/fine-tuning of the base agent.
retrieved_item_representation: Distilled, structured natural-language experiences: concise actionable suggestion lists / workflow guidelines (agent_experience, search_agent_experience), reusable abstract plans (agent_planning), and execution-fix hints. Stored as standardized JSON experience units with a task embedding, goal predicates, action-reasoning pairs, and cross-framework metadata. Surface form injected is distilled strategy/guideline text and adapted workflows, not raw trajectories (raw seeds are never retrieved directly) and not executable code/skills.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Distilled strategy / reusable workflow + state-aware corrective guideline. Planning-stage units are abstract, tool-neutral reusable workflows and generalizable behavioral guidelines (e.g. 'Break down multifaceted questions into smaller constraint checks'); feedback-stage units are diagnostic correction rules tied to observed error patterns. Higher abstraction than raw trajectories; not a procedural executable skill/program.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Disagreement gate (the headline mechanism): G(rho, rho') = 1[cos(phi(rho), phi(rho')) >= beta], beta=0.8, applies a refined plan only if it stays semantically coherent with the original plan, explicitly addressing 'knowledge interference' in cross-framework transfer. Plus: hybrid retrieval (lexical precision + semantic coverage) to reduce mismatched retrievals; refine-time adaptation/tool-substitution to avoid invalid transplanted steps; LLM-ranked deduplication and utility-based eviction to keep high-quality entries. No retriever-aware SFT of the base agent.
memory_type: Structured experience knowledge base / shared cross-framework memory described as hierarchical (workflow-level episodic experiences + execution-pattern semantic knowledge + working memory). Effectively an episodic/workflow experience memory with a semantic experience store and self-evolution; not latent.
write_back: True. Heterogeneous frameworks write distilled experiences back into the shared KB ('write-back across agents'). Construction normalizes both successful and failed runs into structured experience units; at test time pass@2/pass@3 enrich the KB with failure diagnoses. Self-evolving memory performs addition, LLM-ranked deduplication/conflict resolution, and utility-based eviction.
online_growth: True. The KB grows during multi-pass deployment and across frameworks (experiences from one framework instantly available to others via shared APIs; failure diagnoses appended across passes). Fig 5c shows performance scaling with KB size (100 -> 500 examples). It is not frozen after offline induction; it self-evolves (add/dedup/evict).
write_back_trigger: On both success and failure, at construction and across passes. Construction: both successful and failed runs are normalized into experiences (failures yield diagnostic/correction templates). Deployment: feedback-stage failure diagnoses are written into the KB to enrich pass@2/pass@3. Human seeds are curated offline but never retrieved directly. Curation/eviction are reflective (LLM-ranked quality comparison; utility-driven). Not purely on-success.
failure_experience_usage: Success + failure. Failed runs and failure modes are explicitly abstracted into correction templates / diagnostic experiences and retrieved in the feedback stage to apply targeted fixes; human annotators inspect failed logs to build correction templates that seed automatic experience generation. So failures are used correctively, alongside successful workflows.
memory_evolution_update: Add + dedup-merge (conflict resolution) + forget-prune (eviction). New experiences are added; when a candidate is highly similar to an existing entry (max cosine > tau=0.8) an LLM ranker keeps the superior entry (dedup/conflict resolution); under memory pressure an adaptive eviction policy uses a learned per-entry utility score u_j <- u_j + eta(r_j - u_j) balancing recency, frequency, and cross-framework transferability to prune low-utility entries. Entries are effectively curated/overwritten rather than strictly append-only.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No (mostly). Query-time retrieval is fixed BM25 + embedding hybrid top-k (not an RL/learned retrieval policy). There is a learned/adaptive component only in memory management: a per-entry utility score updated by a TD-style rule from reward (retrieval success/execution gain) governing eviction. Case/experience selection itself is similarity-based, not a trained policy (contrast with Memento's M-MDP soft-Q retrieval).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Yes - this is the defining contribution. Agent KB is a cross-framework, plug-and-play shared memory infrastructure: a single KB instance is attached to multiple heterogeneous frameworks (smolagents, OWL, SWE-Agent, OpenHands) via standardized APIs, so experiences gathered in one framework are instantly reusable by others, enabling cross-architecture knowledge transfer without retraining ('collective agent intelligence').
benchmarks: GAIA validation (165 tasks: 53 L1 / 86 L2 / 26 L3); Humanity's Last Exam (HLE) Bio/Chem cleaned subset (149 tasks, multimodal scientific reasoning); GPQA (198 graduate-level MCQs, physics/chemistry/biology, no external tools); SWE-bench Lite (300 GitHub Python issues, 50- and 100-iteration limits). KB constructed from BrowseComp, MultiHopRAG, HLE, WebWalkerQA, RepoClassBench, SWE-Gym-Raw, RepoEval.
benchmark_family: Tool/long-horizon agentic + web research (GAIA); expert/scientific QA (HLE Bio/Chem, GPQA); code repair (SWE-bench Lite). Construction sources add multi-hop QA (MultiHopRAG/HopRAG), web navigation (BrowseComp, WebWalkerQA), and repo-level code (RepoClassBench, SWE-Gym-Raw, RepoEval).
baselines: GAIA: agentic models Search-o1-32B, WebThinker-32B-RL; closed-source frameworks TraseAgent, OpenAI Deep Research, h2oGPTe, Desearch, Alita; open-source frameworks OWL, TapeAgents, AutoAgent, Magnetic-1 (Magentic-One), FRIDAY; and the memory baseline A-MEM (Xu et al. 2025) applied to smolagents. SWE-bench Lite: SWE-Agent and OpenHands base frameworks (vs +Agent KB). HLE: AutoGen, SciMaster, Biomni, OpenHands base. GPQA: Direct Reasoning baselines (o3-mini, Claude-3.7, GPT-4.1) and OpenHands base. Knowledge-type ablation baseline: HANDCRAFTED (student-annotated) vs AGENT KB (auto-distilled). Latency/memory baselines: A-Mem, MemoryBank, ReadAgent.
key_metrics: Reasoning tasks: pass@1/pass@2/pass@3 accuracy (exact-match for GAIA; accuracy for HLE/GPQA). SWE-bench Lite: success/resolution rate at max-iter 50 and 100, plus pass@1/2/3 with budget caps. Efficiency: retrieval latency, memory footprint, per-task token counts and USD cost. Error-category counts (retrieval/planning/reasoning/format/perception/execution).
headline_result: On GAIA, smolagents (GPT-4.1) improve from 55.2% to 73.9% pass@3 (+18.7pp); Claude-3.7 smolagents reach 75.2% pass@3. On SWE-bench Lite, OpenHands (GPT-4.1) gains +4.0pp pass@1 (24.3% -> 28.3%) and up to 45.7% at 100 iters pass@3; OpenHands (Claude-3.7) jumps 30.0% -> 51.0% at 50 iters. HLE: OpenHands 9.5% -> 14.1% (pass@3). GPQA: GPT-4.1 62.6% -> 72.7%. Most-cited: +18.7pp on GAIA pass@3 (smolagents).
ablations: (1) Module ablation (Table 3, smolagents GPT-4.1 on GAIA, baseline 55.15 -> +Agent KB 61.21): removing Refine causes the largest drop (-6.06, back to 55.15), w/o Retrieve -> 57.58 (-3.63), w/o Reason -> 60.00 (-1.21), w/o Planning Stage and w/o Feedback Stage both cap at 59.39; w/ Raw Workflow 58.18 (must adapt, not replay). (2) Retrieval strategy (Fig 5b): hybrid > lexical (BM25) > semantic alone, robust across top-k, optimal at k=3. (3) Disagreement-gate threshold beta sweep (Fig 5a): best at beta ~ 0.8. (4) KB size (Fig 5c): graceful scaling 100 -> 500 examples; code tasks benefit most, advanced reasoning bottlenecked by abstraction quality not quantity. (5) Auto vs handcrafted (Table 4): AGENT KB 75.15% vs HANDCRAFTED 76.97% on GAIA (auto surpasses on L3: 57.69 vs 53.85; SWE-bench 24.33 -> 51.00). (6) Asymmetric cross-domain transfer (Fig 6): reasoning experience helps SWE (37.0%) but SWE experience transfers poorly to reasoning. (7) Error analysis (Fig 7): net error reduction (GPT-4.1 net -10; Claude-3.7 net +11 corrected).
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task metrics (pass@k accuracy / SWE-bench success) are reported; no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / retrieval precision) are reported separately. Retrieval quality is probed only indirectly via the retrieval-strategy and top-k ablations measured by downstream accuracy.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome metrics (pass@k accuracy, SWE-bench resolution). Some process-oriented analysis is included: a manual error-category breakdown (retrieval/planning/reasoning/format/perception/execution) with Venn diagrams of corrected vs newly introduced errors, and progressive pass@1->pass@3 improvement curves, but no formal step-wise reasoning-faithfulness scoring.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Low marginal overhead. GAIA: the retrieval loop adds only ~$0.27 on top of ~$86 per full evaluation run (<0.4%); planning + feedback modules ~317-417 tokens / ~$0.001 each per task vs the ~206k-token action loop. One-off KB construction: ~5.14M prompt + 0.77M completion tokens (~$10.88), amortized. SWE-bench Lite: hinting averages ~$0.0037/issue (<7k tokens, hint length ~88). Latency/memory footprint competitive with A-Mem/MemoryBank/ReadAgent (Fig 4). Reported tradeoff: 4.0-18.7pp gains for ~$3.0-4.5 per task overhead (deemed acceptable).
context_budget_and_selection_count: Default retrieval top-k = 3 (SWE-bench retrieve prompt requests 3-5 entries); reranked-then-deduplicated-then-truncated to top-k. Hyperparameters: hybrid fusion alpha=0.5, dedup similarity tau=0.8, disagreement-gate beta=0.8, eviction learning rate eta. Injected hints are short (SWE-bench hint length ~88 tokens, prompts <7k tokens). Base model fixed to GPT-4.1, temperature 1.0 unless stated. Selection is fixed-k (precision-driven, ablated around k=3), not adaptive per query.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A - this is a method/system paper, not a survey.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A as a benchmark paper. Uses existing benchmarks (GAIA 165, HLE Bio/Chem 149, GPQA 198, SWE-bench Lite 300). For the constructed experience KB (Table 5): BrowseComp 1266->1266, MultiHopRAG 2556->2556, HLE 3000->~2000 (text subset), WebWalkerQA 680->680, RepoClassBench 100->1000 (10 experiences/case), SWE-Gym-Raw 100->1000, RepoEval 100->1000; total ~7802 tasks -> ~9502 experiences, bootstrapped from 80 human seed trajectories.
builds_on: Base agent frameworks smolagents (Roucher/Zhu et al. 2025), OWL (Hu et al. 2025), SWE-Agent (Yang et al. 2024), OpenHands (Wang et al. 2024); retrieval-augmented generation (Lewis et al. 2020); sentence-transformers all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings + BM25; classic CBR Retrieve-Reuse-Revise-Retain cycle (Aamodt & Plaza lineage via Hatalis et al. 2025 review); experience/workflow-memory prior work (Agent Workflow Memory, Synapse, Meta-Agent-Workflow); complementary to DSPy declarative pipelines.
contrasts_with: Single-agent / framework-specific memory systems that cannot transfer across architectures: A-MEM (Xu et al. 2025), MemGPT, MemoryBank, ReadAgent, Learn-by-Interact (single-framework), Agent Workflow Memory, Synapse, and templating pipelines confined to narrow task families. Positioned against these as the first cross-framework plug-and-play shared KB, and against naive experience injection (which causes knowledge interference) via the disagreement gate.
lineage: Group F (decision/experience memory; experience-and-memory-augmented agents). Within the CBR-for-LLM-agents / experience-memory lineage (Reflexion -> ExpeL/AutoGuide -> Agent Workflow Memory/Synapse -> A-MEM/MemGPT), Agent KB is distinguished by being a cross-framework, training-free shared experience infrastructure with a two-stage (planning + feedback) Reason-Retrieve-Refine loop, hybrid BM25+embedding retrieval, self-evolving memory (add/dedup/evict with utility scores), and a disagreement gate to prevent cross-framework knowledge interference. Contemporaneous/sibling to Memento, ReasoningBank, AWM, ExpeL.
